import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source3_18_2", "Source3_18_1"], ["movie_id", "movie_id"]]
# 2) JOIN : [["Source3_18_2", "Source3_18_0"], ["user_id", "user_id"]]

# First join df2 and df1 on movie_id
df_2_1 = pd.merge(df2, df1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Then join the result with df0 on user_id
df_merged = pd.merge(df_2_1, df0[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Now select and reorder columns to match target schema:
# Target Schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Convert columns to required types:
# title: string (already string)
# user_id: float
# movie_id: integer
# rating: float
# timestamp: float
# age: float
# occupation: float

df_merged['user_id'] = df_merged['user_id'].astype(float)
df_merged['movie_id'] = df_merged['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_merged['rating'] = df_merged['rating'].astype(float)
df_merged['timestamp'] = df_merged['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_merged['age'] = df_merged['age'].astype(float)
df_merged['occupation'] = df_merged['occupation'].astype(float)

# Select columns in target order
df_target = df_merged[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# First join Source3_18_2 and Source3_18_1 on movie_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Then join the result with Source3_18_0 on user_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that can serve as keys:
# According to target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]
# Group by: title (string), user_id (float but used as key), movie_id (integer)
# Aggregate the other float columns by average
grouped = join_2.groupby(["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to target CSV
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_18/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
